neighbours.label: the language of epidemiological study methods: enrolment, consent, participation and infection or test status of subjects (refused to participate, consent was obtained, seropositive, HIV infection), as against the same verbs in everyday non-study settings
fire: Of the eligible patients, 18% declined to participate and 4% were lost to follow-up.
Written informed consent was obtained from each participant before sampling.
Children who were seropositive at baseline were excluded from the analysis.
The incidence of hepatitis C infection was higher among injecting drug users.
Mothers were asked to participate in a cohort study of malaria in pregnancy.
Rates of tuberculosis infection were compared between the two districts.
Participants were classified as smear-positive or smear-negative at enrolment.
All subjects consented to provide a stool sample for parasite testing.
quiet: Of the invited families, 18% declined to come and 4% never replied at all.
Written permission was obtained from each parent before the field trip.
Children who were late at the start were excluded from the race.
The number of bicycle thefts was higher near the railway station.
Mothers were asked to bring cakes to the school fair in June.
Rates of rainfall were compared between the two districts.
Runners were classified as junior or senior at registration.
All guests agreed to bring a dish for the potluck dinner.
